drafts.source_identity_policy: Create one generic Form declaration with the existing bound-instance Role whitelist pattern. Do not create one semantic Form declaration per RMEDO Role. Retire CA-R-2684 only after this declaration and the Project-only Scope Unit Declaration Form declaration are both admitted.
drafts.claim: A Scope Delegation is one generic Form used by an externally authored Atom. Its Main Subject is exactly one receiving non-Project Scope Unit. Its Container resolves to that Scope Unit’s one direct declared structural Parent; that containing Scope Unit is the allocator. Project may contain Scope Delegations for its children but cannot be their receiving Main Subject. The Scope Delegation combines the receiving unit’s structural declaration and its assigned contribution in one Atom. Its Role is exactly one of Requirement, Method, Evaluation, Delivery or Operations and identifies the contribution. It records the receiving unit’s existing Name, stable ID, ordered state, optional Label, conditional order.number and direct Parent; it creates no new per-unit fields. The Claim states the assigned contribution and boundaries; the delegating unit retains its full scope and accountability. The generic Form is admitted to the RMEDO Role set by one bound-instance whitelist. Each concrete Scope Delegation Claim lists permitted local HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target selections and local Role/Form pairs. A local Atom is admitted only when its Header.Container-derived IS_CONTAINED_BY target is the receiving Scope Unit, its resolved HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target belongs to a listed selection, and its Role/Form pair is listed. These are Claim statements, not stored whitelist Properties.

whitelists.scope_delegation_main_subject: The single Main Subject is the canonical full Subject string for the specific receiving non-Project Scope Unit. Current Scope Unit Declaration instances use `CAPRMEDIO_STRUCTURE <+ Scope Unit//<Name>`; CA-R-2714 defines the one-string Main Subject field. Project root is excluded and retains its separate Project Declaration.

scope_delegation_role_form_pairs.identity: One generic Form and one owner; no per-Role duplicate Form declarations.

local_requirement_forms.Rule: not a new-model default Form; legacy Rule instance mapping is a later migration decision

local_forms.shared_solution_policy_roles: Settled: Solution, Direct Policy and Approach Policy permit RMEDO Roles (Requirement, Method, Evaluation, Delivery, Operations).

local_main_subject_branches.contract: Each Scope Delegation Claim lists finite allowed HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target selections for local Atoms, plus local Role/Form pairs. Local Atoms must be contained by the receiving Scope Unit through their Header.Container-derived IS_CONTAINED_BY link and their HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target must belong to one listed target selection.
local_main_subject_branches.source_property: Atom.Header.Topics.Main Subject is a single string with cardinality 1 (CA-R-2714); HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT resolves that field to its declared model-entity or instance target (CA-R-2618).
local_main_subject_branches.selection_basis: Use existing typed model-entity and instance selectors to enumerate allowed targets; for Node populations, (Node, Node.**) is an existing selector family. Relation endpoints are declared model entities or instances (CA-R-2486), and HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT is not restricted to Node (CA-R-2618).
local_main_subject_branches.enforcement_limit: Do not infer target admission from Subject text prefixes. Bind or select the actual HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target and require its membership in the Claim-listed selection, together with receiving-unit containment. This is a relation/selector contract, not a new operator or stored whitelist Property.

drafts.semantics: Scope Delegation is admitted in every containing Scope Unit, including Project, so Project may declare children. Each receiving unit is non-Project; Project has no incoming Scope Delegation. The generic Form classifier has one bound-instance RMEDO Role whitelist. Requirement Scope Delegations permit local RMEDO Roles; Method, Evaluation, Delivery and Operations Scope Delegations permit the matching local Role. Solution, Direct Policy and Approach Policy permit RMEDO; Decision permits MEDO only. These are permissions, not a required Role packet. Inherited constraints continue to govern. Local Requirement Forms are Requirement for required outcomes/constraints and existing Declaration families for model definitions; no Rule Form is introduced. Eval Case and Operations Workflow/Step/Action are included. No complete packet or artificial Goal is required.
drafts.tier: No Tier fixed by this Form; Tier rules are owned by the tier lane.
dependencies: The generic Role whitelist is the settled RMEDO set. The bound-instance selector follows the shared Forms lane’s grounded pattern.
Local branch constraints use current HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT endpoint and Header.Container-derived IS_CONTAINED_BY semantics.
drafts.formalization_gate: Use existing typed entity/instance selectors to list allowed HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target populations; require local Atom containment by the receiving Scope Unit through Header.Container-derived IS_CONTAINED_BY. This is a model constraint, not string-prefix matching, a new operator, a new stored whitelist Property, or runtime evidence.
drafts.formal_main_subject_pattern: For each specific unit, author the one scalar value using the established instance path, e.g. `Atom.Header.Topics.Main Subject == "CAPRMEDIO_STRUCTURE <+ Scope Unit//<Name>"`; replace `<Name>` with the declared Scope Unit Name. The pattern is evidenced by live Scope Unit declarations. It is not a wildcard/prefix matcher.

formal_whitelist_claim_template.own_main_subject: For the concrete delegation instance, Main Subject equals the exact current canonical string `CAPRMEDIO_STRUCTURE <+ Scope Unit//<Name>`.

formal_whitelist_claim_template.local_role_form_pairs: Solution, Direct Policy and Approach Policy permit RMEDO; Decision permits MEDO. Each concrete Scope Delegation lists admitted local Role/Form pairs subject to inherited constraints.

drafts.claim: Scope Unit Declaration is the Requirement Form only for the Project-root Scope Unit Declaration. A Scope Unit Declaration Atom has Role Requirement and Form Scope Unit Declaration, and its HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target is a Project Scope Unit. Non-Project Scope Units use the generic Scope Delegation Form. This declaration owns the Form only; the separate cardinality Requirement requires exactly one Project root declaration.

drafts.summary: Establish Project and non-Project Scope Unit declarations and delegations
drafts.source_identity_policy: Create a Requirement/Requirement constraint that replaces old R2688 and R926 coverage without redefining Scope Unit or Atom; their canonical owners remain R2523 and the existing Atom Declaration. Retire the old constraints only after the Scope Delegation and retained Project Form owners are present.
drafts.claim: Every non-Project Scope Unit has exactly one external Scope Delegation whose Main Subject is that Scope Unit. That Atom is the sole external structural authority for its Name, stable ID, ordering state, conditional order.number and direct Parent, and its Claim states one delegated contribution. The Scope Delegation is assigned a single RMEDO Role and its Container resolves to its one direct declared structural Parent, which is the allocator. Ancestors and unrelated external Scope Units are not eligible allocators. Existing model cardinality continues to require exactly one direct Parent for each non-Project Scope Unit and none for Project. Project remains exceptional: retain its one Project-root Requirement/Scope Unit Declaration (currently CA-R-2640), stable Scope Unit ID `CA-SU-00`, unordered state and absence of `order.number`, plus Project-level Requirement/Goal and root Axioms; it has no Scope Delegation. Scope Unit declarations remain authoritative for identity and structural parentage; folder names and physical nesting do not define either. Scope Delegation is admitted by default in every containing Scope Unit, including Project, which may declare child Scope Units. Only the receiving unit must be non-Project; Project itself has no incoming Scope Delegation. Delegation does not erase the delegator’s overall scope or accountability, and no artificial Goal is required to express engineering, evaluation, delivery or operations responsibility. This is a Requirement/Requirement constraint; it introduces no Form or canonical Scope Unit/Atom entity.
drafts.coverage: Combines the scope identity/cardinality structural constraint formerly in R2688 with the non-Project Goal coverage obligation formerly in R926, replacing Goals with one Scope Delegation. It does not absorb Scope Unit kind definition R2523, Project kind R2524, Name/uniqueness/order property declarations, or Tier/Scope Contract rules.

dependencies: A receiving non-Project Scope Unit has exactly one direct structural Parent; the Scope Delegation Container resolves to that Parent. Project may allocate child Scope Delegations and receives none.

drafts.source_identity_policy: Preserve CA-R-924 ID and Summary; keep its existing classification constraint as Requirement/Requirement and add Scope Delegation role/form classifications while retaining the Plan Claim-target qualification.
drafts.claim: The allowed qualified relational Atom types include Requirement/Goal, Requirement/Demand, Plan/Plan and each of Requirement/Scope Delegation, Method/Scope Delegation, Evaluation/Scope Delegation, Delivery/Scope Delegation and Operations/Scope Delegation. A Scope Delegation is relational because its external receiving Scope Unit differs from the defining external Container. A Plan is relational only when its actual Claim target differs under the Relational Atom definition, not because it has decomposition, blocking or a particular Label. This addition does not classify local Solutions, Policies, Decisions, Eval Cases, or executable Operations Forms as relational by topic or filename.
dependencies: Confirm Scope Delegation qualifies under the existing Relational Atom definition at integration; this proposal is claim/subject based, not role-name inference.

drafts.summary: Author Scope Delegations and internal Scope Unit definitions
drafts.source_identity_policy: New identity because CA-M-461 Summary and Claim are explicitly about authoring Declarations and Scope Contracts; do not silently repurpose them. Replace with a general Method/Direct Policy authoring method, without requiring per-Scope-Unit local adoption Atoms.
drafts.claim: Author one external Scope Delegation for each non-Project Scope Unit, with the receiving unit as its Main Subject and its direct structural Parent as Container and allocator. Preserve its structural Name, ID, ordering state and direct Parent, and state the actual R, M, E, D or O contribution in that Role. Do not author a separate external Goal to stand in for an engineering, evaluation, delivery or operations contribution. This is common authoring guidance and requires no local adoption Atom. Inside a unit, define its own Tier-0 realization under the separately admitted Tier/Form rules; do not create a Scope Contract or a mandatory Role packet. Keep the Project root declaration, Project Goal and root Axioms distinct. Derived folder names and paths are not per-unit declaration values; direct structural parentage comes from the declared model, not physical nesting.
drafts.coordination: Tier/Form classification remains with the tier and shared-forms lanes; this Method does not define those Forms or their Tier constraints.
dependencies: A non-Project unit’s direct declared structural Parent is its Scope Delegation allocator.
drafts.form_rationale: Method is included in both MEDO and RMEDO shared-Form candidates; Direct Policy states the common authoring method and does not require each Scope Unit to add a local adoption Atom.

formalization_gates.issue: Validate claim-level allowed active-subject targets and receiving-unit containment
formalization_gates.evidence: CA-R-2618 defines HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT as the Atom-to-resolved-entity-or-instance Relation and permits targets beyond Node; CA-R-2486 permits typed entity/instance endpoints; CA-R-2508 derives IS_CONTAINED_BY from Header.Container; CA-R-2523 defines direct parent containment and exactly one parent for non-root Scope Units.
formalization_gates.action: Each Scope Delegation Claim lists typed permitted HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT target selections and local Role/Form pairs, requires local atoms to be contained by its receiving unit, and binds its own Container to the receiver’s direct structural Parent. This uses existing model operators/relations; the proposal does not claim runtime enforcement.
